x: The 1991 New Economic Policy was a response to a severe balance-of-payments crisis, when foreign reserves covered only about two weeks of imports.
t: Recall the trigger for the 1991 reforms.

x: Both are true: stabilisation was the short-term part of the 1991 reforms because it worked on the demand side, curbing inflation and macroeconomic imbalances quickly. R explains A.
t: Discriminate stabilisation from structural adjustment.

x: Option B is incorrect: after 1991, agriculture's share of GDP fell, as services grew. Forex reserves, FDI and India's share of world exports all rose.
t: Watch for a reversed trend.

x: 1951 is the IDR Act (licensing), 1956 the Industrial Policy Resolution (public sector lead), 1991 the New Industrial Policy (de-licensing), and 2000 the SEZ Policy. The answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Arrange the policies in time order.

x: All three are correct: globalisation linked India to the world economy through trade, FDI and technology flows, and drew in more multinational companies.
t: Recall the elements of globalisation.

x: Both are true: the SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000, under globalisation, to make exports competitive and attract FDI.
t: Recall the SEZ Policy date.

x: Both are true: liberalisation reduces domestic controls, and it does this through de-licensing, freer imports and more room for the private sector. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the tools explain the aim.

x: De-licensing abolished industrial licensing for most industries, import liberalisation cut tariffs and quantitative curbs, disinvestment sold government equity in PSEs, and globalisation integrated India with the world economy, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Define each 1991 reform tool by what it actually changed.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) De-licensing
(b) Import liberalisation
(c) Disinvestment
(d) Globalisation

List-II
(i) Abolition of industrial licensing for most industries
(ii) Reduction of tariffs and quantitative restrictions
(iii) Sale of government equity in public sector enterprises
(iv) Integration of the domestic economy with the world economy

x: All three are correct: LPG means liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation. Globalisation included cutting import duty on capital goods, and liberalisation reduces restrictions.
t: Recall the LPG model.

x: Both are true: structural adjustment is long-term and works on the supply side, reforming industrial, trade, financial and investment structures.
t: Discriminate stabilisation from structural adjustment.

x: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 was the starting point of liberalisation. It ended licensing for most industries.
t: Recall the 1991 starting point.

x: Both are true: liberalisation tools such as lower import duties make domestic manufacturing more competitive because they cut the cost of technology and capital equipment. R explains A.
t: Ask whether lower costs explain competitiveness.

x: The 1948 resolution set up the mixed economy, the 1956 one stressed industrialisation with public and joint sectors, the 1991 policy brought liberalisation, and the SEZ Policy came on 1 April 2000. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each policy to its theme.

x: Option C is incorrect: the SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000. 24 July 1991 is the New Industrial Policy.
t: Match each policy to its date.

x: Both are true: fiscal policy is made up of taxation, spending and public debt, and its aims are growth, jobs, price stability and equity. Its aims do not explain what it is made of, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether aims explain components.

x: Both are true: the 1991 New Industrial Policy began liberalisation, and lower import duty on capital goods was one of its tools.
t: Recall the liberalisation tools.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the IDR Act (1951) set up licensing, V.P. Singh brought the Long-Term Fiscal Policy (1985–86), and SEZs aim at a level playing field for exporters. III is false because the 1956 resolution favoured the public sector, not free trade.
t: Match each policy to its theme.

x: The first Industrial Policy Resolution came in 1948. 1956 is the second, and 1991 the New Industrial Policy.
t: Arrange the policies in time order.

x: Both are true: the New Industrial Policy is linked to LPG, and LPG stands for liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation. Expanding the short name does not explain the link, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether an expansion explains a link.

x: All four are correct: stabilisation is short-term and works on demand, while structural adjustment is long-term and works on supply.
t: Discriminate stabilisation from structural adjustment.

x: Free trade means reducing or removing trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas. The other options are SEZ objectives.
t: Discriminate free trade from SEZ aims.

x: One SEZ objective was an internationally competitive business environment. Licensing and the mixed economy belong to older policies.
t: Recall the SEZ objectives.

x: The LPG reforms opened the door to multinational corporations. Licensing, the joint sector and public-sector dominance belong to the pre-1991 policies.
t: Discriminate pre- and post-1991 features.

x: A high capital-output ratio means more capital is needed to make each unit of output, so capital is less productive.
t: Remember: high COR means low capital productivity.

x: Option D is incorrect: a low COR means less capital is needed per unit of output, so capital is more productive. Needing more capital per unit means a high COR.
t: Remember: high COR means low capital productivity.

x: Economist Raj Krishna coined 'Hindu rate of growth' for India's slow growth of about 3.5% a year before the 1980s.
t: Recall who coined the term.

x: Option D is incorrect: the Hindu rate of growth was about 3.5% a year, not 5.5%. It describes the 1950s to the early 1980s.
t: Recall the rate of 3.5%.

x: All four go with the Hindu rate of growth: Raj Krishna coined it, it was about 3.5%, it covered the 1950s to early 1980s, and it belongs to the pre-reform planning era.
t: Recall the features of the Hindu rate of growth.

x: An industrial corridor combines industry with connectivity, an economic corridor moves goods and services, a dedicated freight corridor is rail freight, and an NIMZ is a large manufacturing area. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each corridor to its meaning.

x: Option C is incorrect: large developed areas built for world-class manufacturing are NIMZs. An economic corridor eases the movement of goods, services and economic activity.
t: Discriminate corridors from NIMZs.

x: Option D is incorrect: dedicated rail freight lines are freight corridors. NIMZs, under the National Manufacturing Policy (2011), are large areas of land developed for manufacturing.
t: Discriminate corridors from NIMZs.

x: Both are true: with a high COR, even high savings may give slow growth, because each unit of investment yields relatively little output. R explains A.
t: Ask whether COR explains slow growth.

x: Maharatna status gives large, high-performing CPSEs more autonomy and financial and managerial powers, so they can expand and compete globally.
t: Recall the purpose of Maharatna status.

x: Both are true: Maharatna lets selected Navratnas compete globally because it gives them more autonomy. R explains A.
t: Ask whether autonomy explains the aim.

x: All three are correct: Maharatna status depends on turnover, net worth and net profit thresholds.
t: Recall the Maharatna criteria.

x: Option B is incorrect: BHEL became a Maharatna in 2013, not 2010. The category itself was created in 2010.
t: Discriminate the category year from a company's year.

x: Maharatna is a status for selected CPSEs, the DPE administers it, BHEL received it in 2013, and Oil India was later upgraded from Navratna. The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: BPCL and HPCL are both Maharatna CPSEs. BEL, NALCO and NMDC are Navratnas, and the Department of Public Enterprises is a government department, not a CPSE.
t: Eliminate pairs containing a Navratna or a non-CPSE.
s: Which one of the following pairs consists of CPSEs that both have Maharatna status?

x: All four are Maharatnas: Power Grid, PFC and REC hold the status, and HAL was upgraded in October 2024 to become the 14th Maharatna.
t: Recall the latest Maharatna additions, including HAL in 2024.
s:
Which of the following CPSEs currently have Maharatna status?
I. Power Grid Corporation
II. Power Finance Corporation
III. REC
IV. HAL

x: All four are Maharatnas: GAIL, Coal India, IOCL and NTPC.
t: Recall the Maharatna list.

x: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) became the 14th Maharatna in October 2024. Oil India was upgraded from Navratna in 2023 as the 13th, while GAIL and BHEL have been Maharatnas since 2013.
t: Recall the most recent upgrades to Maharatna in order.
s: Which CPSE became India's 14th Maharatna in October 2024?

x: Both are true: IOCL and Power Grid Corporation are both Maharatna CPSEs.
t: Recall the Maharatna list.

x: I, II and IV are correct: Maharatna helps Navratnas compete globally, is run by the DPE, and uses net profit as a test. III is false because Maharatna was introduced in 2010.
t: Recall the Maharatna year, 2010.

x: The Department of Public Enterprises runs the scheme and is not itself a CPSE. PFC, ONGC and SAIL are Maharatnas.
t: Find the item that is not a company.

x: Option C is incorrect: BEL is a Navratna, not a Maharatna. MTNL and NALCO are also Navratnas.
t: Discriminate Navratnas from Maharatnas.

x: Both are true: Navratna gives CPSEs more autonomy, and its purpose was to help them compete globally. The purpose does not explain the powers, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a purpose explains the powers.

x: Both are true: turnover, net worth and net profit decide the category, and the categories are Miniratna, Navratna and Maharatna. Naming the categories does not explain the criteria, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether category names explain criteria.

x: Both are true: Maharatna gives more autonomy than Navratna, and it began in 2010, Navratna in 1997. Their start dates do not explain the difference in powers, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether dates explain powers.

x: Both are true: Navratna and Maharatna are categories of CPSEs, and Maharatna began in 2010.
t: Recall the CPSE categories.

x: A is true and B is false: BHEL is a Maharatna, but NALCO is a Navratna.
t: Discriminate Navratnas from Maharatnas.

x: Navratna began in 1997 with 9 CPSEs, Maharatna in 2010, and the three categories are Miniratna, Navratna and Maharatna. The answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: All four are Maharatnas: BHEL makes heavy electrical equipment, SAIL is the largest public sector steel maker, ONGC explores for and produces oil and gas, and NTPC is the largest power generator, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each Maharatna to its core business.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) BHEL
(b) SAIL
(c) ONGC
(d) NTPC

List-II
(i) Heavy electrical equipment manufacturer
(ii) Largest public sector steel producer
(iii) Oil and natural gas exploration and production
(iv) Largest power-generating utility

x: All four are Navratnas: BEL, NALCO, MTNL and RINL.
t: Recall the Navratna list.

x: Three are criteria: turnover, net worth and net profit. Competing globally is the aim of the status, not a criterion.
t: Discriminate criteria from aims.

x: Tarapore I (1997) dealt with capital account convertibility, Tarapore II (2006) with fuller convertibility, Narasimham I (1991) with the financial system, and Narasimham II (1998) with banking sector reforms, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Use the years to separate the two Tarapore and two Narasimham reports.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Tarapore Committee – I
(b) Tarapore Committee – II
(c) Narasimham Committee – I
(d) Narasimham Committee – II

List-II
(i) Banking Sector Reforms, report 1998
(ii) Fuller Capital Account Convertibility, 2006
(iii) Capital Account Convertibility, 1997
(iv) Financial System, report 1991

x: Option B is incorrect: Vijay Kelkar headed the Kelkar Task Force. Raja Chelliah headed the Chelliah Committee on tax reform.
t: Match each committee to its chair.

x: Raja Chelliah headed the 1991 Tax Reforms Committee, Vijay Kelkar's 2002 task forces covered direct and indirect taxes, his later committee (2015) reviewed the PPP infrastructure model, and Malhotra dealt with insurance reform, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Separate the 1991 tax committee from the 2002 Kelkar task forces.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Chelliah Committee
(b) Kelkar Task Force
(c) Kelkar Committee
(d) Malhotra Committee

List-II
(i) Insurance Sector Reforms
(ii) PPP Infrastructure Model
(iii) Tax Reforms Committee, 1991
(iv) Task forces on direct and indirect taxes, 2002

x: The Rangarajan committees covered financial inclusion, sugar decontrol and PSU disinvestment, and Malhotra covered insurance reform. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: Goswami dealt with industrial sickness, Janakiraman with the stock-market scam, Vaghul with the call money market, and Abid Hussain with de-reserving small-industry items. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: Abid Hussain chaired the committee on de-reserving items kept for small-scale industry.
t: Match each committee to its chair.

x: Both are true: Janakiraman looked into the 1992 securities scam, and Vaghul into the call money market.
t: Match each committee to its subject.

x: Vaghul dates from 1987, Narasimham I from 1991, Narasimham II from 1997 (report 1998), and Raghuram Rajan from 2008. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Arrange the committees in time order.

x: C. Rangarajan chaired three: financial inclusion, sugar and disinvestment. The Malhotra Committee was chaired by R.N. Malhotra.
t: Find the committee with a different chair.

x: Vijay Kelkar headed the Kelkar Task Force, Onkar Goswami the committee on industrial sickness, R.N. Malhotra the insurance reform committee, and R. Janakiraman the securities scam inquiry, giving a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii.
t: Match each committee to the chairman it is named after.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Kelkar Task Force
(b) Goswami Committee
(c) Malhotra Committee
(d) Janakiraman Committee

List-II
(i) Vijay L. Kelkar
(ii) R. Janakiraman
(iii) R.N. Malhotra
(iv) Onkar Goswami

x: Two dealt with financial-sector reform: Narasimham I (1991) and Raghuram Rajan (2008). Narasimham II dealt with banking, and Vaghul with the call money market.
t: Discriminate financial-sector from banking-sector reform.

x: Both are true: Onkar Goswami chaired the committee, and it dealt with industrial sickness. Its subject does not explain who chaired it, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a subject explains a chair.

x: N. Vaghul chaired the Vaghul Committee on the money market (1987). Narasimham, Abid Hussain and Tarapore chaired other committees.
t: Match each committee to its chair.
